packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
FIRST READER RESPONSE - PACKET 05
Unverified image-only reading. UTF-8 plain text.

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification of the work or author was revealed to me before or during reading. My standing context contains a generic memory index that mentions a "Fragmentarium" project and archival work, but nothing naming this text, author or reading.
- The images themselves show modern pencil notes, which I report as observations only: "Stams, STA, Frg. 210-1r" (image-009), "Stams, STA, Frg. 210-1v" (image-018), "Stams, STA, Frg. 210-2r" (image-027), "Stams, STA, Frg. 210-2v" (image-035); also "aus I/70 (Weihnachtnais?) 1670" (image-008), "aus I/71 (Mais? 1670)" (image-021), "29.VI." (images 006, 014), "11 Juni" (image-034). I did not use these to identify anything.
- I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..036 (ls of the packet directory to get filenames and pixel sizes; packet.json was not read). No web or search tools used. All 36 images loaded.

PACKET STRUCTURE
Four faces, each = one reduced overview + eight native tiles (2 columns x 4 rows, overlapping):
  Face A: overview image-001, tiles 002-009 (pencil label "...210-1r")
  Face B: overview image-010, tiles 011-018 (label "...210-1v")
  Face C: overview image-019, tiles 020-027 (label "...210-2r")
  Face D: overview image-028, tiles 029-036 (label "...210-2v")
Line numbers below are counted from the first text line at the top of the face as seen in the overview image; I give the tile(s) where each line was actually read. Tile overlaps were collapsed (repeated lines not double counted).

CONVENTIONS: (abc) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [...] = lost/cropped/outside the leaf; - at line end = word continues.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
- Single leaves of parchment (one bifolium-half each?), heavily trimmed and folded as binding waste: folded flaps on all sides, sewing/turn-in creases, nail/tack holes. Faces C/D have a large burn/rodent-like hole in the lower centre; a clear plastic spatula lies across part of C and D in the photographs.
- Two columns of text, Gothic textualis, ca. 29-31 lines per column, brown ink, ruled in drypoint/lead. On every face one column is partly cut by the trimmed edge or the fold (A: col b cut at right; B: col a cut at left; C: col a cut at left and destroyed lower right of col b; D: col b cut at right, lower col a destroyed).
- Red rubrics and red/red-and-pen initials: "Quinta." (A col a), "Tertia. Lectio." and "Quarta." (B), "Undecima." (C col a), a red "Jo..." and a large red I (both D col b), "In nat(ali) sancti Joh(annis) bap(tiste)" (D col b), red initials Q (A col a, 2 lines; A col b large Q with long tail), B (B col b), I (D col b), Q (D col b), S (D col b).
- Ink-rubricated (touched) capitals within lines at sentence starts (Et, Placuit, Beati, Ecce, Habet, Decebat, Petrus, Non, Melius, Ille, Dum, Omnis, Cum, Sed, Unde, Maiorem, Hoc).
- Running numeral at top margin of Face C above col a: "xxxiii" (lower margin area of image-020). Small correction "ei" interlinear (C col a), "cum" interlinear (C col b).
- Tentative interpretation (not identification): consecutive numbered lessons (Tertia, Quarta, Quinta ... Undecima) of a homily/sermon text in liturgical lectionary form; Face D col b moves from a Gospel pericope opening "In illo tempore. Dixit [Ihesus]..." to a collect-like prayer and a rubric for a following feast. Faces B (Tertia/Quarta) precede A (Quinta) in text sequence, i.e. the leaf labelled 1v appears to read before 1r, or the labels are reversed - reported, not resolved.
